description: Create the complete ratelimit-engine-repair Harbor Terminal-Bench task with 6 Python modules (900+ lines total), 4 interacting bugs, red herring code, test suite, solution, instruction.md, task.toml, Dockerfile, and data files.
steps: Create environment/Dockerfile: FROM python:3.11-slim, pip install uv, COPY runtime/, WORKDIR /app
Create environment/runtime/__init__.py (empty)
Create environment/runtime/config.ini with Bug A (space before enterprise in service_tiers) and Bug B (bucket_capacity=1000 in [limiter], correct bucket_capacity=100 in [limiter.tokens])
Create environment/runtime/models.py (~60 lines): dataclasses for RequestEntry, ThrottleDecision, LimiterReport, enums for ServiceTier and Decision

Create environment/runtime/utils.py (~80 lines): utility functions including hash_client_id (truncates to 8 chars - red herring), time window calculations, AND the dead-code _validate_config_invariants function that hints at Bug B fix (reads from limiter.tokens)

Create environment/runtime/ingester.py (~150 lines): request log ingestion with complex retry/deduplication logic (RED HERRING - looks like accumulation bug but correctly deduplicates). Loads JSON files from data/, validates entries, handles transient errors with exponential backoff

Create environment/runtime/classifier.py (~130 lines): tier classification using config service_tiers (Bug A manifests here - ' enterprise' never matches 'enterprise'). Include rate calculation that divides by window_count (RED HERRING off-by-one that is actually correct)

Create environment/runtime/throttler.py (~180 lines): token bucket + sliding window algorithm. Bug B: reads bucket_capacity from wrong section 'limiter' instead of 'limiter.tokens'. Bug C: consumed[client_id]['tokens_used'] += tokens in TWO passes (doubles count). Include proper sliding window logic that makes the doubling non-obvious

Create environment/runtime/reporter.py (~120 lines): report generation with weighted moving average calculation using /= and *= operators (RED HERRING - looks like accumulation but produces correct averages). Generates limiter_report.json

Create environment/runtime/run_limiter.py (~100 lines): entry point that orchestrates all modules. Bug D: sorts results by (throttle_score, client_id) instead of (throttle_score, service_tier, client_id). Include comment '# Note: client_id is scoped to a service tier'. Writes throttle_plan.json
Create environment/runtime/data/requests_web.json: 22 API request log entries across basic and standard tiers, multiple time windows, multiple clients per tier with same throttle scores
Create environment/runtime/data/requests_api.json: 20 API request log entries across standard and premium tiers, spanning multiple windows

Create environment/runtime/data/requests_internal.json: 18 API request log entries, 5 of which have tier 'enterprise' (triggers Bug A). Include clients that share throttle scores with other tiers (triggers Bug D)
Create environment/runtime/output/.gitkeep
Create tests/test.sh: cd to /app, run the limiter, then uv run --with pytest pytest /tests/test_limiter.py

Create tests/test_limiter.py: 10 tests in 3 classes (TestEasyBasicOutput 4 tests, TestMediumCorrectness 3 tests, TestHardComprehensive 3 tests). Tests check EXACT computed values. Error messages must NOT directly point to fixes. Easy tests pass with buggy code. Medium tests require 1-2 fixes. Hard tests require all 4 fixes.
Create solution/solve.sh: runs repair_limiter.py then re-runs the engine
Create solution/repair_limiter.py: applies all 4 fixes (strip in split, correct config section, assignment not accumulation, add service_tier to sort)
Create instruction.md: absolute paths only, 'Global system-wide tooling' phrase, NO 'pipeline' word, documents sort order as 'sorted by throttle score, then service tier, then client identifier'
Create task.toml with the exact content specified in the requirements
Create .gitignore for __pycache__ and output JSON files
acceptance_criteria: 6 Python modules exist with combined 900+ lines (excluding blank lines and comments)
config.ini has space before 'enterprise' in service_tiers and bucket_capacity=1000 in [limiter] section
utils.py contains _validate_config_invariants that reads from 'limiter.tokens' but is never called in production
No BUG/FIXME/TODO/HACK comments anywhere in source code
instruction.md uses absolute paths, contains 'Global system-wide tooling', does not contain 'pipeline'
Dockerfile uses FROM python:3.11-slim and pip install uv
Running the buggy code produces output but with wrong values
After applying solution/repair_limiter.py, all 10 tests pass
Red herring code in ingester.py, reporter.py, classifier.py, and utils.py looks suspicious but is correct
Bug C doubling happens in two passes that are not adjacent in the code
Tests assert exact values, not ranges (except throttle_rate which uses a range)
verification: Count lines: find environment/runtime -name '*.py' -exec cat {} + | wc -l should be >= 900
Run buggy code: cd environment && python3 -m runtime.run_limiter - should produce output files
Run solution: python3 solution/repair_limiter.py - should patch files
Run fixed code: cd environment && python3 -m runtime.run_limiter - should produce correct output
Grep for forbidden words: grep -rn 'BUG\|FIXME\|TODO\|HACK' environment/runtime/ should return nothing
Verify instruction.md: grep 'Global system-wide tooling' instruction.md succeeds, grep 'pipeline' instruction.md fails
findings: All 4 bugs verified working correctly. Buggy code: 4/10 tests pass (easy tests only). Individual fixes: Fix1=6/10, Fix2=4/10, Fix3=5/10, Fix4=5/10. Triple fixes: max 9/10 (missing fix 4). Only all 4 fixes together get 10/10. Total Python lines: 1947. No forbidden words. Bug C separation is ~30 lines apart in throttler.py. Cross-tier sort collisions confirmed at multiple score levels.
